sentences.text: PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL ALONG WITH M.F.A.CROB. COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.
The Insurer has filed MFA.No.4318/2019 and the claimants have filed MFA.Crob.60/2021 challenging the compensation awarded for the death of T.S.Omkaramurthy, a 21 year old.
2. The Insurer contends that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased himself and therefore, the Tribunal was in error in attributing negligence only on the driver of the lorry.

3. The claimants, on the other hand, contend that the finding of the Tribunal that the driver of the lorry was responsible for the accident cannot be found fault with and also contended that the sums awarded under different heads by the Tribunal were on the lower side.
4. It is not in dispute that the accident resulted in the death of T.S.Omkaramurthy.
In order to establish that the deceased had contributed to the accident, the Insurer did not choose to examine either the driver of the lorry or any other eye witness.
The Tribunal, taking note of the fact that the charge sheet had been laid against the driver of the lorry, has rightly come to the conclusion that it was the driver of the lorry who was negligent.
5. As far as compensation is concerned, the Tribunal has assessed the notional income of the deceased at Rs.12,000/- per month and awarded a sum of Rs.17,28,000/- towards loss of dependency.
However, the Tribunal has not added future prospects to the notional income.

In the light of the judgment in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED Vs. PRANAY Cholamandalam Ms General Insurance vs Shivaprasad on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165956779/
4 SETHI & OTHERS - AIR 2017 SC 5157, 40% requires to be added to the income towards future prospects, which makes the income of the deceased to be Rs.16,800/-.

sentences.text: Since the deceased was a bachelor, 50% requires to be deducted out of the said income, which makes the income of the deceased to be Rs.8,400/-.

6. As a consequence, the claimants would be entitled to Rs.18,14,400/- (Rs.8,400/- X 12 X 18)
towards loss of dependeny.

7. The claimants, being the parents and brother, would be entitled to Rs.44,000/- each i.e.,
Rs.1,32,000/- towards loss of consortium.

In addition, they would also be entitled to Rs.33,000/-
under conventional heads.

8. Thus, the claimants, in modification of the impugned award, would be entitled to the following sums:
 Sl. Amount  Particulars  No. (In Rs.)
 1. Loss of Dependency 18,14,400/-

2 . Loss of Consortium 1,32,000/-
 3. Conventional Heads 33,000/-
 Total 19,79,400/-
9.

Accordingly, the claimants would be entitled for compensation of Rs.19,79,400/- as against Rs.18,18,000/- awarded by the Tribunal, along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
10. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
11. The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transferred to the Tribunal.
12. The apportionment of compensation shall be in terms of the award of the Tribunal.

However,
claimant No.3 i.e., the brother of the deceased would be entitled to Rs.44,000/- only.
The appeal of the Insurer as well as cross objection of the claimants are accordingly disposed off.
